title: event
description: A product event: CloudEvents 1.0, structured JSON, with the distributed tracing extension. One standard shape for every product, readable by any tool that knows CloudEvents (ADR-E1), and linked to the request that caused it (ADR-E6).

specversion.description: The CloudEvents version, always 1.0, so a CloudEvents reader knows how to read the rest (ADR-E1).

id.description: The event's id, unique within its source. A client whose stream dropped sends the last id it had as Last-Event-ID, and the server resumes after it (ADR-E3).

source.description: Where the event comes from, as /<product-id>/<thing>. It names the product and the served thing, so a reader listening to many products (control-room) knows where the change happened (ADR-E2).

type.description: What happened, as <product-id>.<thing>.<verb>, the verb in the past tense. A reader picks the events it handles by type, and each type has its own schema listed in its product's events.asyncapi.yaml (ADR-E2, ADR-E4).

subject.description: The id of the thing the event is about, inside the source, so a reader knows which one changed (ADR-E2).

time.description: When it happened, as an RFC 3339 time, so a reader can order events and show when a change took place (ADR-E1).

datacontenttype.description: Always application/json: data is JSON, so a reader parses it without asking (ADR-E1).

data.description: What happened; its shape is the event's own schema. The envelope leaves it open, so every event shares one envelope and adds only its own data (ADR-E4).

traceparent.description: W3C trace context: the request that caused the event. It links the event to its trace in OpenTelemetry, so a person can follow an event back to what caused it (ADR-E5, ADR-E6).

tracestate.description: W3C trace state, vendor data that travels with the trace. It rides beside traceparent so a tracing system keeps its own data across the event (ADR-E6).
